questions.q: What makes a URL action different from every other action type covered in this chapter?
options: It's the one action type that reaches outside the workbook entirely, sending a click or hover to an external web address
It's the only action type that can use a Select trigger
It's the only action type available on Tableau Public
It cannot use field values from the clicked mark
questions.explain: URL actions send a viewer's interaction to a web address — optionally built dynamically using <Field Name> placeholders from the clicked mark — while every other action in this chapter stays inside the workbook.

questions.q: What does a parameter action let a viewer do?
options: Set a parameter's value by clicking or hovering on a mark, instead of using a parameter control like a dropdown or slider
Permanently delete a parameter from the workbook
Change the dashboard's overall size
Convert a parameter into a calculated field automatically
questions.explain: A parameter action lets a click or hover on a mark set a parameter's value directly — a more natural interaction model than requiring the viewer to find the matching value in a dropdown.

questions.q: In the Add Set Action dialog, what two separate behaviors does the dialog ask you to define?
options: What happens when the action runs (e.g. Assign values to set) and what happens when the selection clears (e.g. Add all values to set)
The dashboard's width and height
The workbook's publish location and permissions
The font and color of the target sheet's title
questions.explain: Set actions uniquely define two behaviors: what happens when the action runs (Assign/Add/Remove values to set) and what happens when the selection clears (Keep/Add all/Remove all values from set).

questions.q: What Chapter 10 and Chapter 11 concepts do set actions and parameter actions build directly on, respectively?
options: Set actions build on sets (custom subsets of dimension members); parameter actions build on parameters (a single referenceable value)
Both build on LOD expressions from Chapter 12
Set actions build on joins; parameter actions build on extracts
Neither builds on any earlier chapter — both are entirely standalone features
questions.explain: This course already covered sets in Chapter 10 and parameters in Chapter 11 — set actions and parameter actions are the dashboard-interaction layer on top of those already-known concepts, not new ideas from scratch.

questions.q: How many action types are available in the Actions dialog's "Add Action" dropdown, in total?
options: Six — Filter, Highlight, Go to URL, Go to Sheet, Change Parameter, and Change Set Values
Two — Filter and Highlight only
Four — Filter, Highlight, URL, and Parameter, with no set or navigation actions
Unlimited — new custom action types can be defined by name
questions.explain: The Actions dialog supports exactly six action types: Filter and Highlight (Lesson 82), Go to URL, Change Parameter, and Change Set Values (this lesson), and Go to Sheet (Lesson 84).
